sections.text:
1 Itaque non ex libro Laurentiano, sed ex archetypo Angelicano descriptus esse
videtur codex Ambrosianus. — Nomine Palchi perperam lecto, Bernardus de
Montfaucon Vetti Valentis opus in hoc volumine exstare credidit. In Diario
Italico, p. 15 (= Bibliotheca Bibliothecarum, t. II, p. 529) notat tres astrologiae
iudiciariae scriptores, inter quos “ Mpalis vel potius Valentis apotelesmatica „
contineri in codice 354 (qui est nunc B 38 sup.). [F. C.]
sections.en: 1 Therefore the Ambrosian codex seems to have been copied not from the Laurentian book, but from the Angelican archetype. — Having read the name Palchi incorrectly, Bernard de Montfaucon believed that the work of Vettius Valens existed in this volume. In the Diarium Italicum, p. 15 (= Bibliotheca Bibliothecarum, t. II, p. 529) he notes three writers of judicial astrology, among whom “the apotelesmatics of Mpalis or rather Valens” are contained in codex 354 (which is now B 38 sup.). [F. C.]

summary.headline: Ambrosian Codices B 38 and B 85
summary.text: Catalog entries for Ambrosian codices B 38 sup. and B 85 sup., describing treatises on zodiac signs, planetary lore, and hidden things, with named authorities including Dorotheus, Apomasar, Masalas, Euclid, Stephanus, Hermes, and Antiochus. The page also records B 38 sup.'s dependence on a faulty exemplar and its close agreement with Florentine codex 11.
